claim: **Definitions.** A test, helper or fixture under `tests/` *uses SQLite* when it does any of these: names a `sqlite` URL; reads a file under `examples/sqlite-demo/`; imports or calls Python's `sqlite3` module or anything in `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite`; calls `sqllens.preflight._probe_sqlite`, or a preflight path that reaches it with a `sqlite` URL; passes `"sqlite"` as a dialect or engine value; or relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union (`load_extension`, or a `sqlite_` or `pragma_` name, a CTE or table so named included). A case relies on such an entry when it runs under a `None` or unknown dialect and its outcome comes from that entry. It also relies on one when, under any dialect, its outcome differs from the `None`-dialect outcome only because the entry is in the union. An example is a `sqlite_`-prefixed data table under dialect `mysql` that proves the configured dialect arrives, as in the MySQL row #382 gave `test_with_widgets_hides_introspection_result_under_configured_dialect`. Naming ChromaDB's `chroma.sqlite3` file is not a use. A use is *SQLite-only* when the behaviour it asserts exists only for SQLite. That covers at minimum: the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite` package, `sqlite_path_from_url` and `_readonly_uri`; the SQLite preflight probe; a `sqlite`-keyed entry of a per-dialect table in `src/sqllens/safety/` or in the system prompt (for example `sqlite_master`, `pragma_*` names, `load_extension`); `sqllens init`'s SQLite template; `claude-desktop install`'s SQLite file-stem naming; a case that relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union; and a `sqlite` case whose expected outcome differs from the same test's `mysql` case with the same other inputs. A use whose classification is unclear counts as SQLite-only, and its test also gets a MySQL version. A `sqlite` URL used only as the non-MySQL input that a MySQL-only check refuses (`tests/unit/test_rule_set_file.py::test_non_mysql_url_is_refused`, `tests/unit/test_cli_rule_sets.py::test_validate_refuses_a_non_mysql_url`) is engine-neutral where another non-MySQL scheme can reach that check: its replacement passes one, for example `postgresql://u@db.invalid/shop`, straight to `load_rule_sets`, and asserts the same refusal. Where config load refuses every other scheme before the check runs (`sqllens validate`), the use is SQLite-only, and its map row says no MySQL counterpart exists because config load accepts only MySQL and SQLite URLs. Every other use is *engine-neutral*. After the change, every use of SQLite under `tests/` is SQLite-only.

claim: For the dialect cases of every test: - A `sqlite` case with the same other inputs and the same expected outcome as an existing `mysql` case of that test is removed. - An engine-neutral case (as the first criterion defines it) that ran only under `sqlite` runs under `mysql`. Its outcome under `mysql` can differ from its SQLite expectation for two excused causes, and in both the SQLite case stays as SQLite-only: - a `mysql`- or `sqlite`-keyed entry or branch of a per-dialect table or dialect check in `src/`. The MySQL case asserts the code's MySQL outcome. - sqlglot's `mysql` grammar reading the same text differently (for example, `#` starts a comment and a double-quoted name is a string, only under `mysql`). The MySQL case is the input written in MySQL syntax with the same meaning (for example, backticks for a quoted name, or an unparseable statement with no `#`), and it asserts the SQLite case's outcome. An existing `mysql` case of the test that already is that input stands in for it. Any other difference, or one whose cause is unclear, is a defect handled as the last criterion states. - The default `dialect` of `_assert_filtered_and_readonly` in `tests/unit/test_safety_rls.py` is `"mysql"`. - Every `None`-dialect and unknown-dialect case that exists at the merge base still exists. - Each such case that relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union (a SQLite-only case, as the first criterion defines it) has a counterpart in the same test, under each of the dialect values that case uses. The same applies to each case of any dialect that relies on such an entry. The counterpart relies only on a MySQL entry or on MySQL-only syntax (for example `load_file`, `sleep`, a table in the `mysql`, `sys` or `performance_schema` schema, or a statement only the `mysql` dialect reads, such as `# note\nSHOW TABLES`). It asserts the same outcome as the SQLite case. If the code gives the MySQL entry a different outcome, the difference is handled as the last criterion states.
